newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to research mobile phone health risk.
newsitem.headline: EU to research mobile phone health risk.

text.p: More research is needed into whether mobile phones pose a health risk, a group of scientific experts told the European Commission on Wednesday.

"There is no evidence of any health risk emerging from mobile phones, but the results of present research are inadequate to draw firm conclusions on this issue," the experts found, according to a Commission statement.
The Commission said it would decide by the end of the year how to bolster EU research into the effects of radio frequency radiation on health.
The Commission appointed the 10 experts in response to concerns about the safety of mobile phones and of their radio base stations.
Much of the controversy centres on the electromagnetic energy that is generated by cellular phones.
The experts said research was needed in areas such as the interaction of radio telephone emissions with living tissues, genetics, cancer and the immune and nervous systems.
"The Commission will examine how the research plan proposed by the expert group could be implemented and intends to take a decision on this later this year."
